'channel' is chat.Channel that may not be there, so a write off it can't be guaranteed to happen — and nothing in this statement says it might be skipped. Test it first ('if channel == null { ERROR("…") }', or 'if EXISTS(channel)'), or gate on it with a traversal block ('channel-[x:…]-> { … }'), which runs zero times when it's empty. (see handbook: front#maybe-absent)

an 'until' condition is re-evaluated on a timer, so it must be read-only — a 'await' here would act every tick. Keep the condition to reads and 'refresh'; do the effect after the await resolves.

every field of this write to book.Companies is a '?:' fill of a possibly-absent value, so at runtime they can all be omitted and the write reaches the system empty. Gate the write on presence instead (e.g. 'r-[x:…]-> { write … }'), so it only runs when there's something to write.

this side of the ordered comparison may be absent (number (or absent)) — it comes from a branch that might not have run, or an answer that might not be there. Ordering needs a value on both sides: fall back to something that always answers ('COALESCE(…, 0)'), gate on it first ('r-[x:…]-> { … }'), or test it with '==' and order inside that branch. (Equality itself is fine on a maybe-absent value — absent is simply never equal.) (see handbook: front#maybe-absent)
